<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 258|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XIII.}}</noinclude>to vvhom I shal reach the dipped bread. And vvhen he had dipped the bread, he gaue it to Iudas Iscariote Simons sonne. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=27}}† And after the morsel, then Satan entred into him. And {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to him, That vvhich thou doest, doe it quickely. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=28}}† But no man knevv of those that sate at table to vvhat purpose he said this vnto him. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=29}}† For certaine thought, because Iudas had the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christ had some prouision before hand giuen him by the Collections of the faithful, which was vsed both in his owne necessities, & bestowed vpon the poore.}}∷ purse, that {{sc|Iesvs}} had said to him, Bie those things vvhich are needeful for vs to the festiual day: or that he should giue some thing to the poore. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=30}}† He therfore hauing receiued the morsel, incontinent vvent forth. And it vvas night.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=31}}† VVhen he therfore vvas gone forth, {{sc|Iesvs}} said, Novv the Sonne of man is glorified, and God is glorified in him. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=32}}† If God be glorified in him, God also vvil glorifie him in him self, and incontinent vvil he glorifie him. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=33}}† Litle children, yet a litle vvhile I am vvith you. You shal seeke me, & {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 7, 34.''}}* as I said to the Ievves, VVhither I goe, you can not come: to you also I say novv. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=34}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''1. Io. 3, 23.''}}* {{sup|‖}} A nevv commaundement I giue to you, That you loue one an other: as I haue loued you, that you also loue one an other. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=35}}† In this al men shal knovv that you are my disciples, if you haue loue one to an other. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=36}}† Simon Peter saith to him, Lord, vvhither goest thou? {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered, vvhither I goe, thou canst not novv folovv me, but hereafter thou shalt folow. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=37}}† Peter saith to him, VVhy can not I folow thee novv? {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 35. Mr. 14, 29. Lu. 22, 33.''}}* I vvil yeld my life for thee. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=38}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} answered him, Thy life wilt thou yeld for me? Amen, amen I say to thee, the cocke shal not crovv, vntil thou denie me thrise.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XIII.}}}}

''5. Began to vvash.'') This lotion was not onely of curtesy, such as the Iewes vsed tovvard their ghests, nor onely for example of humilitie: but for mysterie and signification of the great puritie that is required before we come to receiue the holy Sacrament, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Puritie required to the receiuing of the B. Sacrament.}}which straight after this washing was to be instituted and giuen to the Apostles. ''Ambr. li. 3 de Sacra. c. 1 Bernard. de cœna Domini Serm. 1''.

''10. To vvash his feete.'') The foulnes of the feete, when al the rest is cleane, signifieth the earthly affections and relikes of former sinnes remitted: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Venial sinnes taken avvay by sacred ceremonies.}}which are to be cleansed by deuout actes of charitie & humilitie, as ''S. Ambrose li. 3 de Sacr. c. 1''. and ''S. Augustine ep. 108. & tract. 56 in Io''. do note. And because this was onely a ceremonie, & yet had such force, both now and afterward vsed of the Apostles, that it purged smaller offenses and filthines of the soule, as ''S. Ambrose'' and ''S. Bernard'' gather, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ambr. & Bern. locis citatis''.}}it may not seeme strange that holy water and such ceremonies may remit venial sinnes.

''14. You also ought.'') Our Maister neuer spake plainer, nor seemed to commaund more precisely, either of Baptisme or the Eucharist or any other Sacrament: and yet by the Churches iudgement<noinclude>{{rh|||directed}}</noinclude>
